findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher never checks the grant shortcut (wrong offset and inverted condition)
findings.body: The encoded ID is `ssttgg:uuid`, so the grant shortcut is at indexes 4..6 (`substring(4, 6)`). The matcher uses `substring(3, 5)`, which spans the last char of the token type and the first char of the grant. It then does `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, which rejects a match instead of a mismatch. The two mistakes cancel out: the check can never fail, so `expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` only verify the `xxxx:<uuid>` shape. If a grant type put the wrong shortcut in the token ID, the tests would still pass. Fix by comparing `items[0].substring(4, 6)` and returning false when it does NOT equal the expected shortcut. The failure message in `describeTo` is also not meaningful.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId actually checks grantType
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` repeats the grantType check, so `rawTokenId` is never validated. A null `rawTokenId` is accepted silently, and `encodeTokenId` would then emit a token ID ending in the literal string "null" (e.g. `onrtac:null`) instead of failing fast. It should be `requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of a NullPointerException, not the intended validation
findings.body: In `before()`, the factory's `sessionFactory` is never set (it stays null). Decoding `ofrtac:5678` misses "ac" in `grantsByShortcuts`. `getGrantTypeByShortcut` then falls into the 'refresh maps' branch and calls `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`, which throws an NPE. The test catches any `RuntimeException`, so it passes on that NPE rather than on the `IllegalArgumentException` the decoder is supposed to throw for an unknown grant type. The test does not verify the real behavior. It should catch `IllegalArgumentException` specifically and provide a usable session factory, or the refresh fallback should be made testable.

findings.title: Access token is tagged ONLINE even when the session is converted to offline right after
findings.body: The session type is derived from `userSession.isOffline()` at access-token creation time. In authorization-code and ROPC flows with `offline_access`, the access token is created first from the online user session. Only afterwards does `generateRefreshToken()` create the offline session, and the online session is then removed (`FIRST_OFFLINE_ACCESS` and ROPC handling in `OAuth2GrantTypeBase`/`ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType`). That access token gets an `on` prefix, but its `sid` points to a session that no longer exists as online, and only the offline session remains. The stated purpose of the PR is to let endpoints look up only the correct session type. For these tokens the encoded session type would point at the wrong (non-existent) session type. The offline_access case should be considered when computing the session type, or the limitation should at least be documented.

findings.title: Grant shortcuts are not validated (null or length != 2)
findings.body: `postInit` inserts `gtf.getShortcut()` into a `ConcurrentHashMap` without validating it. A third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` returning null causes an NPE during server startup. A shortcut that is not exactly 2 chars makes tokens encode fine, but `getTokenContextFromTokenId` then throws `IllegalArgumentException` because it requires the context part to be exactly 6 chars. The existing duplicate check only covers collisions, and the lazy refresh paths in `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` skip validation too. Add an explicit startup check that every shortcut is non-null and exactly 2 characters, with a clear error message.

findings.title: New abstract method breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added as an abstract method to a provider SPI interface. Any custom grant type factory compiled against the previous version fails to compile and, if already built, throws `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls it. Since the encoder already has an 'na' fallback, a default implementation would keep existing extensions working. If it is intentionally mandatory, this breaking change should be called out in the upgrade notes.

findings.title: Javadoc says 3-letter shortcut, but implementation requires exactly 2 characters
findings.body: The Javadoc says the shortcut is 'usually like 3-letters', yet all factories use 2-letter shortcuts and the decoder (`encodedContext.length() != 6`, fixed 2-char slices) only works with exactly 2 characters. Someone implementing a custom grant following the Javadoc and using 3 letters would produce token IDs that cannot be parsed. The contract should state 'exactly 2 characters'.

findings.title: Access token `jti` format change is user-visible but undocumented
findings.body: Access token IDs (`jti`, also logged in the `token_id` event detail) change from a plain UUID to `<6-char context>:<uuid>`. Clients, log pipelines, or custom extensions that assume the `jti` is a UUID will behave differently. This PR adds no release/upgrade note or documentation for the new format or the new `tokenContextEncoder` SPI, so operators have no notice of the change.
